text: Sixty-eight year old female, sudden left-sided weakness, husband says she was normal at one forty.
58 yom c/o crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, started 40 minutes ago while shoveling snow.
facts: crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm
notes: 'c/o' treated as standard medic report shorthand, not an explicit 'patient says' attribution, so role medic (utterance not tagged attribution).

text: Medic 14 to Valley Medical, we're en route with a stroke alert, ETA eight minutes.
notes: 'stroke alert' is a system activation, not a stated complaint; no complaint.chief (labeling it would be the 'suspected stroke' inference the guide forbids).

text: On exam she's got a mild right facial droop, right arm drifts, right leg holds fine, no gaze deviation, she's following commands and her speech is clear.
notes: Positive exam findings are also listed under stroke.deficits (guide uses 'facial droop' as a deficit phrase). 'following commands and her speech is clear' -> aphasia/agnosia 0; 'leg holds fine' -> leg 0.

text: 86 yof, ground level fall, caregiver found her on the bathroom floor this morning, unknown down time.
notes: 'caregiver found her on the bathroom floor' matches the guide's 'found on the floor' -> onset_witnessed false even though this is a fall call; caregiver = family per section 3. 'this morning' is when she was found, not onset, and down time is unknown -> no symptom.onset.

text: 67 yom, COPD exacerbation, sats 84 percent on room air, RR 32, tripoding with pursed lip breathing.
She was totally fine when I talked to her at 9 am, then her neighbor called me and said she couldn't get her words out.
speaker: daughter
notes: Daughter on mic gives LKW (family). The word-finding deficit is explicitly relayed from the neighbor, so clause-level attribution makes it bystander rather than the speaker's default role.

text: D-stick reads 38, patient is responsive to voice only, cool and diaphoretic.
RACE is, uh, face two, arm two, leg one, gaze one, aphasia two, so total of eight.
notes: Scores only; RACE total 8 has no key; no deficit phrases stated so no stroke.deficits.

text: It feels like an elephant is sitting on my chest, it started when I was walking the dog, maybe half an hour ago?
speaker: patient
notes: Patient on mic. 'Elephant sitting on my chest' labeled as the chief complaint (chest pressure). Onset 'maybe half an hour ago?' is hedged -> no symptom.onset; 'when I was walking the dog' is a circumstance, not a time.

text: Copy, meeting you there.
Patient says she tripped over the dog and fell, denies hitting her head, denies any loss of consciousness.
notes: Fall stated by patient -> complaint 'fall' (guide example). Both denials yield no facts.

text: seventy four yom slurred speech in right sided weakness wife found him like this in the recliner
notes: 'in' read as ASR error for 'and'. 'wife found him like this' -> onset_witnessed false, role family. No RACE items (no exam described).

text: Nursing home patient, 91 yof, temp 101.8, heart rate 118, BP 88 over 50, resps 24, sats 90 percent on two liters nasal cannula, skin warm and flushed, foley bag is cloudy, we're headed to Mercy General, ETA twelve.
notes: 101.8 F -> 38.8 C. 'foley bag is cloudy' and 'nursing home patient' are patient/setting findings, not explicit scene observations -> no scene.notes. No complaint stated.

text: Husband thinks maybe she was okay around eleven last night, but he went to bed early so he's not sure.
notes: Hedged LKW ('thinks maybe', 'not sure') -> no fact.

text: BP one forty two over eighty eight, pulse one oh four, resps twenty, sats ninety six on room air.
Sixty-one yof, c/c altered mental status, confused and disoriented to time and place, sugar one twenty two, no diabetic history.
notes: 'no diabetic history' has no key.

text: Left facial droop, left arm drift, eyes deviated to the right, last known well 10 pm per son.
notes: Findings stated as observed exam findings: unqualified 'facial droop' -> 2 per guide, 'arm drift' -> 1, 'eyes deviated to the right' -> gaze 1. 'per son' governs only the LKW clause.

text: Obvious deformity to the right hip, shortened and externally rotated, CMS intact distally.
notes: Hip deformity is an exam finding, not a stated complaint; no key fits.

text: He was fine at dinner, uh, six thirty, and then he just slumped over at the table, I saw the whole thing.
speaker: son
notes: Son on mic: 'fine at dinner, six thirty' -> LKW 6:30; 'I saw the whole thing' -> witnessed. 'slumped over' not labeled as a deficit.

text: He's used his ProAir like four times since dinner and it's not doing anything, he can barely talk.
speaker: mother
notes: ProAir -> albuterol. 'can barely talk' describes respiratory distress, not a stroke deficit, and no complaint is named.

text: Pressure's one sixty over, sorry, one sixty-eight over ninety-four.
She's got weakness in the right arm and leg, and her speech is kind of garbled.
notes: 'kind of garbled' hedges severity, not presence -> labeled. No RACE items: weakness and garbled speech are not RACE-scorable wording.

text: She's allergic to shellfish and she had shrimp at dinner, her lips started swelling fifteen minutes ago.
speaker: husband
notes: Husband on mic. Lip swelling treated as the stated presenting complaint.

text: Can you grab the stair chair and the drug box off the rig?
Pt denies blood thinners, NKDA, home meds are lisinopril and Lipitor, no head strike.
notes: 'Pt denies' governs only the blood-thinner clause; NKDA and home meds are unattributed -> medic. Lipitor -> atorvastatin. 'no head strike' has no key.

text: He took two of his nitro before you got here and it didn't help at all.
speaker: wife
notes: Wife on mic; home nitro taken -> nitroglycerin.

text: GCS 14, E4 V4 M6, pupils PERRL, c-collar applied.
notes: M6 stated -> gcs_motor 6. GCS 14 / V4 not converted to ACVPU (confusion not stated).

text: RACE five, um, face one, arm two, leg one, no gaze deviation, aphasia one.
Wife says he's been short of breath for three days, worse tonight, and he ran out of his home oxygen yesterday.
notes: 'Wife says' governs the whole sentence. Running out of home oxygen yesterday does not state current oxygen status -> no vitals.on_oxygen.

text: He's a type one diabetic, takes Lantus at night and Humalog with meals, and he skipped dinner tonight.
speaker: wife
notes: Lantus -> insulin glargine, Humalog -> insulin lispro. 'type one diabetic' has no key.

text: BP 210 over 110, correction, 201 over 110, heart rate 88, glucose 132.
She tripped on the curb and fell and hit her head on the sidewalk, but she never passed out.
speaker: bystander
notes: Bystander on mic. Not labeled stroke.onset_witnessed: the bystander never says they saw it, and it is a fall, not a symptom onset. Denial of passing out -> no fact.

text: Hx of MI with two stents, takes Plavix, metoprolol and Lipitor, allergic to morphine.
notes: Plavix (clopidogrel) is an antiplatelet, not on the guide's anticoagulant list -> no meds.anticoagulant.

text: last known well 2 30 per daughter and daughter says she takes elequis
notes: 'elequis' read as ASR spelling of Eliquis -> apixaban.

text: BGL was 42, gave an amp of D50, recheck is 156, now A and O times four.
notes: Two distinct glucose measurements (before and after D50), not a correction, so both labeled. D50 is a treatment given, not a home med.

text: uh were gonna package her up and move now my partners driving
Arm score is two, she can't lift the right arm at all, leg is a one.
Facility nurse says she's been more confused than baseline since yesterday, foley in place, urine cloudy and foul smelling.
notes: Guide has no role for a facility nurse; treated as family because the guide groups caregivers with family and she speaks as the patient's caregiver (knows baseline). 'More confused than baseline' = new confusion -> C. Foley/urine findings have no key.

text: BP one ten over seventy, uh, wait, one oh two over seventy, heart rate one eighteen, skin pale cool and clammy.
Placed on CPAP at 10, sats coming up to 92, wet crackles in all fields.
notes: CPAP treated like the guide's non-rebreather: an oxygen delivery device, so on_oxygen true. '10' is CPAP pressure, not liters.

text: Maybe a slight droop on the left side of her face, hard to tell with her dentures out.
notes: Hedged ('maybe', 'hard to tell') -> no facial RACE item and no deficit.

text: fifty two year old female chest tightness and nausea since three a m very diaphoretic
Bystanders say she seized for about two minutes, she's postictal now, only responding to voice.
notes: 'Bystanders say' governs only the seizure clause. The two-minute seizure length is a duration, not an onset time. 'only responding to voice' is the medic's observation -> V.

text: No facial droop, arms and legs are strong with no drift, speech is normal, eyes midline.
glucose 5 hundred and 12 pt says he ran out of his metformin last week
notes: '5 hundred and 12' -> 512. 'ran out of his metformin' still names his own prescribed medication, so it is labeled in meds.list with role patient.

text: Twelve lead done at fourteen thirty two, ST elevation in two, three and aVF, I'll attach it to the ED report.
notes: 'I'll attach it' is future intent -> no ecg.attached. ST-elevation findings have no key.

text: Pt is on Lovenox shots since his knee replacement, lac to the forehead, bleeding controlled.
notes: 'Pt is on' is not a 'patient says' attribution -> medic. Lovenox -> enoxaparin. Forehead laceration is an exam finding, not labeled as a complaint.

text: Change of plans, Mercy's on stroke divert, we're going to St. Joseph's instead, new ETA twenty two.
notes: Mercy is on divert, not the destination.

text: She takes Xarelto and something for her thyroid, she's allergic to penicillin, and she fell getting out of the tub.
speaker: husband
notes: Husband on mic. 'something for her thyroid' names no drug, so it is not in meds.list.

text: Stroke alert, 81 year old male, LKW 0630, RACE of 7, he's on Eliquis per the wife, BP 196 over 104, glucose 118, going to Regional, ETA 14 minutes, please have CT ready.
notes: LKW '0630' written in colon form as 24-hour '06:30' (guide gives no 24-hour example). 'per the wife' governs only the Eliquis clause. 'Stroke alert' is not a complaint; 'RACE of 7' is a total with no key.

text: seven year old male audible weezing sats ninety one percent heart rate one forty mom thinks he might have a peanut allergy
notes: Peanut allergy hedged ('thinks he might') -> no allergies fact. 'audible wheezing' is an exam sign, not a stated complaint.

text: She's usually alert and chatty, but today she only opens her eyes when you pinch her.
speaker: caregiver
notes: Caregiver on mic (family). 'only opens her eyes when you pinch her' = responds to pain -> P.

text: Right arm drifts down in about five seconds, left arm holds without drift.
notes: RACE arm is scored on the affected (right) side: drifts within 5 s -> 1. Normal left arm not labeled as a separate 0 because there is only one arm key.

text: HR 42, sinus brady, BP 84/50, pale and diaphoretic, A&O x3.
Witness says he fell off the ladder, maybe ten feet, and he's not sure if the guy's on blood thinners.
notes: Witness = bystander. Fall height is hedged but has no key anyway. The witness is unsure about blood thinners -> no anticoagulant fact.

text: Leg, uh, she can't lift the left leg off the bed at all, and the arm's the same.
notes: 'the arm's the same' -> arm also can't lift -> 2.

text: Allergic to sulfa and codeine, full code per the daughter.
notes: 'per the daughter' governs only the code-status clause; allergies unattributed -> medic.

text: Resps are, um, twenty eight, twenty eight and labored, sat's eighty nine on two liters nasal cannula, gonna bump him to a non-rebreather.
notes: Moving to a non-rebreather is future intent and does not change the labels.

text: Eyes are looking to the right, and she doesn't recognize her left arm, doesn't even know she's weak.
notes: Recognizes neither the arm nor the deficit -> agnosia 2.

text: Stroke team's been notified, they'll meet us in CT.
Sugar's forty-eight, uh, no, eighty-four, I read it upside down.
sixty two yof a phasic right arm is flaccid polst on the fridge says dnr
notes: 'a phasic' read as ASR for 'aphasic' -> 2 (guide example). 'flaccid' -> arm 2. The medic read the POLST, so code status is medic. The POLST's location on the fridge is an explicit scene observation, like 'walker by the bed'.

text: Describes it as pressure, eight out of ten, doesn't radiate, denies shortness of breath or nausea.
notes: Describes an unnamed pain ('it') and gives denials; no complaint is stated.

text: MVC, restrained driver, moderate front end damage, airbags deployed, self-extricated and ambulatory on scene.
notes: MVC treated as the chief complaint, by analogy with the guide's 'fall'. Vehicle damage, airbag deployment and extrication are explicit scene observations.

text: Temp one oh three point one tympanic, pulse one thirty, pressure's soft, eighty over, no, ninety over sixty.
notes: 103.1 F -> 39.5 C. The '80 over' is corrected to 90/60.

text: Wife witnessed the onset, says he dropped his coffee cup at 7:15 and couldn't get a word out.
notes: The information comes from the wife -> family. The witnessed onset time is labeled as symptom.onset, not LKW (not phrased as 'fine/normal at'; equating them would be inference).

text: Satting 88 on 4 liters, correction, 6 liters, still 88.
notes: The correction changes only the flow rate (4 -> 6 L), which has no key. SpO2 is 88 either way.

text: Unresponsive, GCS 3, sugar 29.
notes: GCS 3 implies M1, but the motor score is not stated -> no gcs_motor.

text: daughter says she's been dragging her left leg and dropping things with her left hand sense this morning
notes: 'sense' read as ASR for 'since'. These are history from the daughter, not an exam -> no RACE items.

text: Mom's on Coumadin and she hit her head pretty hard on the nightstand.
speaker: daughter
notes: Daughter on mic. The head strike is the stated presenting event (the mechanism, like 'fall'), so it is labeled as the complaint.

text: Twelve lead is attached to the report, time on it is 10:47.
No known allergies, meds are Synthroid, Norvasc and a baby aspirin daily.
notes: Synthroid -> levothyroxine, Norvasc -> amlodipine, baby aspirin -> aspirin (antiplatelet, not an anticoagulant).

text: ETA is 15, um, make that 18 minutes, traffic's backed up on 101.
seventy nine year old woman with right sided facial droop and aphasia on cumadin for a fib lkw nine fifteen
notes: Unqualified 'facial droop' -> 2 and 'aphasia' -> 2, mapped the same as the guide's 'aphasic'; both are explicitly stated findings. 'cumadin' read as ASR for Coumadin -> warfarin. 'a fib' has no key.

text: Temp ninety five point four, she was on the floor all night, room air sat ninety one.
notes: 95.4 F -> 35.2 C. 'on the floor all night' does not say she was found, so no onset_witnessed (that would be inference).

text: Eighty two, sorry, seventy two year old male, right facial droop, slurred speech.
notes: Age corrected from 82 to 72. Unqualified facial droop -> 2. Slurred speech is dysarthria, not aphasia -> no aphasia item.

text: I don't take any blood thinners, and I'm not allergic to anything.
speaker: patient
notes: Patient on mic, with explicit denials.

text: shortness of breath started an hour ago history of chf takes lasix and eloquis
notes: 'eloquis' read as ASR for Eliquis -> apixaban; Lasix -> furosemide. 'chf' history has no key.

text: Patient says he took his insulin this morning but hasn't eaten anything, he's a little confused but answering questions.
notes: 'Patient says' governs the insulin/eating clause only. 'a little confused' is the medic's observation -> C.

text: 34 year old female, c/o lower right abdominal pain since yesterday, vomiting times three, temp ninety nine point six.
notes: 99.6 F -> 37.6 C. 'c/o' -> role medic (same call as v1_002).

text: Numbness and tingling in her right hand and face, started twenty minutes ago.
facts: numbness and tingling in right hand and face
notes: Focal sensory symptoms treated as a deficit rather than a chief complaint, following the guide's 'left-sided weakness' example. No RACE items.

text: Neighbor says he's been drinking since noon and fell off the porch steps.
notes: Neighbor = bystander. 'drinking since noon' is not a symptom onset.

text: Engine 6 on scene, one patient, requesting ALS.
Found down by the neighbor this morning, last seen normal at 10 pm per the neighbor.
notes: The neighbor found the patient and gave the LKW -> bystander for both.

text: Heart rate one twenty, correction, one ten, still in a fib.
Temp one oh two point four, resps twenty six, sats ninety three on room air, crackles in the right base.
Son says she's been vomiting for two days, now she's unresponsive, sugar reads HI on the meter, breathing deep and rapid.
notes: 'Son says' governs only the vomiting clause; 'now she's unresponsive' is the medic's observation. The glucose reading 'HI' is not an integer -> no vitals.glucose. 'deep and rapid' breathing has no number.

text: She passed out in the checkout line, the cashier thinks she's diabetic, maybe on insulin, but isn't sure.
notes: The syncope is stated without attribution -> medic. The cashier's diabetes and insulin statements are hedged -> no facts.

text: Pupils equal, grips unequal, weaker on the right, no other deficits noted.
facts: grips unequal, weaker on the right
notes: Grip strength is not a RACE item -> no exam.race.arm.

text: Wife thinks his sugar was around sixty earlier but she's not sure, he's awake and talking now, A&O x4.
notes: The wife's sugar estimate is hedged -> no glucose. A&O x4 -> A.

text: C-collar on, sats ninety eight on a non-rebreather, resps twenty four and shallow.

Stroke scale, facial palsy is, um, a one, mild, arm and leg both zero, no gaze deviation, speech is slurred, she's on Pradaxa per her daughter, sugar is ninety four, BP one seventy eight over ninety, and she's A&O times four.
notes: The aphasia/agnosia item is not scored: slurred speech is dysarthria, and A&O x4 is not a RACE aphasia finding. 'per her daughter' governs only the Pradaxa clause; Pradaxa -> dabigatran.

text: Patient states he took two baby aspirin at home, didn't touch the pain.
notes: Aspirin the patient took at home is labeled as a med taken. 'didn't touch the pain' names no complaint.

text: Gave 324 of aspirin chewed and one nitro sublingual, pain's down to a five.
notes: Aspirin and nitro were given by EMS (treatment, not home meds). A pain score has no key.

text: LKW two thirty, sorry, correction, two fifteen per husband.
notes: Corrected from 2:30 to 2:15.

text: Wife is showing me his out-of-hospital DNR, it's signed and dated, he's comfort care.
notes: The medic is looking at a signed out-of-hospital DNR, so this is a medic observation even though the wife is presenting it. 'comfort care' maps to no extra key.

text: transporting emergent too good sam eta eleven
notes: 'too' read as ASR for 'to'. Destination title-cased as said: 'Good Sam'.

text: Speech is fine, face symmetric, no drift in either arm, but the left leg drifts down and hits the bed.
notes: 'drifts down and hits the bed' -> leg 1: the guide's 'drift' wording applies, and the leg was lifted against gravity, so it is not 'can't lift' (2). Gaze not mentioned.

text: Lights and sirens to Regional, we're about ten minutes out, can you have a bed ready?
notes: 'about ten minutes out' is a normal ETA estimate, not a hedge on the fact -> 10.
